title: Projectile velocity evolution through rising, apex and falling states

authority_basis.claim_scope: Repository-backed SBA04 atom tracks vx, vy and gravity through rising, apex and falling states.

concepts.statement: In the standard no-drag projectile model, horizontal velocity remains constant while vertical velocity changes linearly under constant downward gravity.
concepts.why_required: The learner must track the velocity vector as a changing state rather than reuse the launch vector everywhere.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Apex and falling-state questions can be solved with the wrong component signs or a changing horizontal velocity.

concepts.statement: At the apex the vertical velocity component is zero, while horizontal velocity generally remains nonzero and gravitational acceleration remains downward.
concepts.why_required: The apex is a component event, not a stop event or zero-acceleration event.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: The whole velocity or gravity may be incorrectly set to zero at the apex.

symbols.name: horizontal velocity component at time t
vertical velocity component at time t

model_conditions.condition: Projectile is modelled after release with zero horizontal acceleration and uniform downward gravitational acceleration.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The component evolution equations follow from the standard no-drag constant-g model.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Drag, propulsion or nonuniform gravity changes the component evolution.

representations.semantic_geometry: A rising-to-apex-to-falling trajectory sequence shows constant vx, changing signed vy, tangent velocity arrows and a persistent downward gravity arrow at every stage.
must_not_imply: total velocity is zero at the apex
acceleration becomes zero at the apex
representations.verification_method: Check vx is unchanged across panels, vy changes sign through zero, and g remains downward in every panel.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Declare axes, frame and the shared post-launch clock before interpreting component signs.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Velocity signs can be interpreted in an unstated frame or time origin.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Evolve vx and vy separately using the standard component relations.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The learner may change both components together or reuse launch components unchanged.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Treat the apex as the event v_y=0 while retaining v_x and downward g.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Apex can be mis-modelled as zero total velocity or zero acceleration.

required_transformations.description: Translate motion stages into signed vx/vy states while keeping gravity distinct from velocity.
Use evolved signed components to recognize an apex or later-flight velocity event, solve the requested state, and verify the event condition.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: The projectile's whole velocity is zero at the apex.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The vertical component is zero there and is often described as the projectile momentarily stopping upward motion.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A projectile with nonzero horizontal launch component continues moving horizontally through the apex.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show a horizontal tangent velocity arrow at the apex while vy is labelled zero.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Only vy is zero at the apex; vx remains u_x in the standard model.
misconceptions.verification: Evaluate v_x(t_apex)=u_x and confirm it is nonzero for an oblique launch.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Gravitational acceleration becomes zero at the apex because vertical velocity is zero.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Velocity and acceleration are often conflated when one instantaneous component vanishes.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Immediately after the apex the projectile begins falling because downward acceleration persisted through the apex.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Keep the same downward g arrow before, at and after the apex.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: The velocity state vy=0 does not alter the model law a_y=-g.
misconceptions.verification: Differentiate v_y=u_y-gt to recover constant a_y=-g at all times.

problem_families.name: Projectile velocity components at a time or event
problem_families.first_technical_move: Write the two velocity components in the declared frame before forming any magnitude or direction.
fatal_errors: setting total velocity to zero at apex
